messages.subject: weird error when adding ggvis code
parts: Hi! I had a shiny app that worked properly and then I decided to add some ggvis graphics. So when i just introduced a piece of ggvis code into server.R and tried to run the app, I immediately got an error message saying "invalid assignment for reference class field ‘n’, should be from class “numeric” or a subclass (was class “environment”)". Interestingly, this error message appeared twice on my app page - in the main panel and in the sidebar panel instead of fileInput. Does anyone have a clue what has gone wrong? Eventually, please tell which specific details / pieces of code you might need to answer the question. Thank you in advance!

parts:
Hi Winston! Thanks for your reply. So I tried two options:

Option #1

library(shiny)
library(shinyIncubator)
library(googleVis)
library(ggvis)
library(dplyr)

shinyServer(function(input,output,session){

# many reactive functions here

MI<-reactive({
    if (is.null(input$taxtax)) {
      return(NULL)
    }
   
    progress <- Progress$new(session, min=1, max=10)
    on.exit(progress$close())
   
    progress$set(message = 'Calculating MI',
                 detail = 'Please wait...')
   
    for (i in 1:10) {
      progress$set(value = i)
      Sys.sleep(0.05)
    }
   
    # functions to calculate two vectors called "mivector" and "treats"
    # example of "mivector": c(1.5,2,2.5,2,2.5,3,2.5,3,3.5)
    # example of "treats": c("A","A","A","B","B","B","C","C","C")

    if (length(which(mivector>0))==0) {
      plot(0,type="n",axes=F,xlab="",ylab="")
      text(x=0.5,labels="MI and MI2-5 values could not be plotted as free-living nematodes are absent in your sample.")
      text(x=0,labels="Scroll down to see the PPI plot.")
    } else {
      plotdf<-data.frame(mivector,treats)
     
      plotdf<- plotdf %>% group_by(treats) %>% summarise(mimean=mean(mivector),misd=sd(mivector))
      plotdf<-rbind(mutate(plotdf,mibar=mimean-misd),mutate(plotdf,mibar=mimean+misd))
      plotdf<- plotdf %>% select(-misd) %>% arrange(treats)
      for (i in 1:length(levels(plotdf$treats))) {
        eval(parse(text=paste("bar",i,"<-plotdf$mibar",sep="")))
        eval(parse(text=paste("bar",i,"[-which(plotdf$treats==levels(plotdf$treats)[i])]<-mean(plotdf$mimean[which(plotdf$treats==levels(plotdf$treats)[i])])",sep="")))
        eval(parse(text=paste("bar",i,".treat<-rep(levels(plotdf$treats)[i],nrow(plotdf))",sep="")))
        eval(parse(text=paste("plotdf<-cbind(plotdf,bar",i,",bar",i,".treat)",sep="")))
      }
     
      command<-""
      for (i in 1:length(levels(plotdf$treats))) {
        command<-paste(command,"layer_paths(~bar",i,".treat,~bar",i,",strokeWidth:=2) %>% ",sep="")
      }
     
      eval(parse(text=paste("plotdf %>% ggvis() %>% layer_points(~treats,~mimean) %>% ",command,'scale_numeric("y", domain = c(0, 5)) %>% add_axis("y",grid=F) %>% add_axis("x",grid=F) %>% bind_shiny("MIplot")',sep="")))
    }

   })
})


Option #2 (introducing the ggvis code without reference to reactive output, just to try if it works at all)

  plotdf<-rbind(mutate(plotdf,mibar=mimean-misd),mutate(plotdf,mibar=mimean+misd))
  plotdf<- plotdf %>% select(-misd) %>% arrange(treats)
  for (i in 1:length(levels(plotdf$treats))) {
    eval(parse(text=paste("bar",i,"<-plotdf$mibar",sep="")))
    eval(parse(text=paste("bar",i,"[-which(plotdf$treats==levels(plotdf$treats)[i])]<-mean(plotdf$mimean[which(plotdf$treats==levels(plotdf$treats)[i])])",sep="")))
    eval(parse(text=paste("bar",i,".treat<-rep(levels(plotdf$treats)[i],nrow(plotdf))",sep="")))
    eval(parse(text=paste("plotdf<-cbind(plotdf,bar",i,",bar",i,".treat)",sep="")))
  }
 
  command<-""
  for (i in 1:length(levels(plotdf$treats))) {
    command<-paste(command,"layer_paths(~bar",i,".treat,~bar",i,",strokeWidth:=2) %>% ",sep="")
  }
 
  eval(parse(text=paste("plotdf %>% ggvis() %>% layer_points(~treats,~mimean) %>% ",command,'scale_numeric("y", domain = c(0, 5)) %>% add_axis("y",grid=F) %>% add_axis("x",grid=F) %>% bind_shiny("MIPLOT")',sep="")))
 
})
